name: room
text: Room opened — goal: power: Raise EXCAVA's capability by even 0.5%: find new tools, best/newest models, combine elemen

name: Gearbox
text: Add InstantX-ComfyUI’s depth-aware upscaler to EXCAVA’s pipeline. It sharpens fine details in still frames by using depth maps to guide upscaling, which directly improves visual clarity without adding motion artifacts. The trade-off is a slight increase in compute time per frame, but the quality gain outweighs the cost for high-stakes outputs.

name: Torque
text: Depth-aware upscaling won’t fix EXCAVA’s motion blur—it’s a temporal artifact, not a spatial one. The real risk is wasted effort: we’d burn cycles on a tool that doesn’t address the core problem. Instead, test VFI-Flow’s motion reconstruction first; if it cuts blur by 0.5%+, it’s the better lever. Settle it with a side-by-side A/B on 100 frames: blur metrics don’t lie.

name: Gearbox
text:
Add VFI-Flow to EXCAVA’s motion pipeline. It reconstructs motion blur into sharp frames by filling gaps in motion vectors, directly attacking the core temporal artifact Torque flagged. The trade-off is a 10-15% slowdown per frame—worth it if it delivers even a 0.5% quality bump. Skip depth upscaling; it’s a spatial fix for a motion problem.

name: Torque
text: VFI-Flow’s 15% slowdown isn’t the real risk—its motion reconstruction introduces temporal artifacts that could distort fine details more than the original blur. Instead, test a hybrid: run VFI-Flow *only* on high-motion segments (flagged by optical flow variance) and keep the rest of the pipeline unchanged—this caps the compute hit while isolating the fix’s impact. Settle it with a blind A/B test: measure motion blur reduction *and* detail retention in the same clips before and after, no cherry-picking.
